mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital for corporations and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1% (as measured by rolling 20-day returns over 5 years).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 9.0% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 9.0% for two consecutive months, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a contraction in housing demand and rising cost pressures, which together signal a weakening economy and negative equity returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST decline and CPIAUCSL rise) fails to predict negative SPX 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases (measured by Rank IC < 0.03 over 5-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below 95.0), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to reduced corporate output and earnings, leading to negative returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is below 95.0, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 225.0 indicates accelerating inflation, which may prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 225.0, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, indicated by a high payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 131,000 thousand, supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS is above 131,000 thousand (over 5-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) combined with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in consumer and housing demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (RSAFS decline and HOUST drop) fails to predict negative SPX 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 0.1%) for more than 3 months indicates an extended period of monetary accommodation, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is below 0.1% for 3+ months, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases over the last 10 years.
